name: MI355X, MLPerf Inference v6.0 Offline multi-node: Llama 2 70B WMXFP4 on 87xMI355X across 11 nodes
model: Llama 2 70B (WMXFP4 weights, FP8 KV cache, UINT8 scales)
methodology: AGGREGATE, MLPerf Offline scenario at cluster scale: 87 GPUs across 11 nodes (AMD's system id is 87xMI355X_22xEPYC_9575F, i.e. 22 EPYC 9575F hosts). Samples per second 3629.98. TP size is not stated as a single number in the log because the multi-node submission uses a distributed SUT over ZMQ with workers on all nodes rather than one TP group; the source states device_count equals the total healthy GPUs across the cluster. Assume large-scale TP/EP spanning all 11 nodes. Software: same per-node stack as the single-node submission (PyTorch 2.9.1+git8907517, ROCm 7.0.0, vllm-11b6af52, aiter-6af8b687). Model: Llama 2 70B WMXFP4, FP8 KV cache, UINT8 scales, from amd/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf-WMXFP4-AMXFP4-KVFP8-Scale-UINT8-6.0MLPerf-GPTQ. OMITTED BY SOURCE: exact TP size, number of replicas vs one giant TP group, network fabric and topology, input/output sequence lengths. Reproducible is false at this scale: the repro guide describes the procedure but 11 nodes is not something an individual can re-run.
notes: This is the 'first MLPerf submission over one million tokens/sec' figure AMD headlines for Llama 2 70B in the Closed division. AMD reports 93% scaling efficiency for Offline and Server and 98% for Interactive on this 11-node run. The paired Server-scenario number for the same cluster is 1016375 tok/s at 3591.83 samples/s, from the same source - recorded separately rather than here to avoid conflating scenarios. The single-node 8-GPU figure is 103480 tok/s (mi355x-mlperf-v6-0-llama2-70b-wmxfp4-offline-tokens); 87/8 = 10.9x more GPUs for 10.07x the throughput, which is the arithmetic behind AMD's 93% claim.
